source: Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada (RTC); Las Vegas Monorail Company / LVCVA
license: Public records; RTC publishes ridership in annual reports
notes: Ridership figures are approximate. RTC publishes system-wide totals in annual reports but per-route breakdowns are not consistently available. Route-level estimates below are derived from: (1) RTC annual ridership reports, (2) Nevada Legislature transportation committee testimony, (3) Clark County Regional Transportation Plan documents. Figures marked 'estimated' use proportional allocation from system totals and service frequency data.

rtc_bus_routes.name: The Deuce
rtc_bus_routes.description: Las Vegas Blvd (Strip) — full length from Downtown Transportation Center to South Strip Transit Terminal
rtc_bus_routes.ridership_source: Estimated from RTC FY2023 annual report system total (~57,000 daily systemwide); Deuce is consistently cited as highest-ridership fixed route, ~35-40% of Strip corridor ridership. Pre-COVID (FY2019) Deuce+SDX combined ~32,000 daily; post-COVID recovery estimated at ~65% of pre-COVID by 2023.
rtc_bus_routes.event_day_notes: Major events on The Strip cause severe overcrowding and frequency supplementation. RTC deploys additional buses for major stadium/arena events.

rtc_bus_routes.name: SDX — Strip & Downtown Express
rtc_bus_routes.description: Limited-stop express: South Strip Terminal → Downtown; fewer stops, faster than Deuce
rtc_bus_routes.ridership_source: Estimated at ~25-28% of Deuce ridership based on service frequency ratio and stop density. RTC does not publish separate SDX ridership.

rtc_bus_routes.name: Route 115 — Hacienda/Industrial
rtc_bus_routes.description: Connects South Strip / Allegiant Stadium area to Downtown. Primary RTC service to Allegiant Stadium district.
rtc_bus_routes.ridership_source: Estimated from RTC route ridership data presented in Clark County Regional Transportation Plan (2019). Post-Allegiant opening, ridership likely increased on event days. Baseline non-event daily ridership estimated at 3,000-4,000.
rtc_bus_routes.event_day_notes: RTC supplements Route 115 with game-day express shuttle service on Raiders game days. Event express service (direct from Strip hotels) is operated separately under contract and not counted in regular ridership.

rtc_bus_routes.name: Route 108 — Paradise Road
rtc_bus_routes.description: Paradise Rd corridor — serves LVCC, University District, Virgin Hotels Las Vegas
rtc_bus_routes.ridership_source: Estimated from RTC systemwide data; Paradise Rd is a major employment corridor. Convention week ridership significantly elevated.

rtc_bus_routes.name: Route 201 — Tropicana Ave
rtc_bus_routes.description: East-West: Tropicana Ave from Western Ave to Nellis Blvd; serves UNLV / Thomas & Mack, Orleans Arena
rtc_bus_routes.ridership_source: Estimated from RTC data; Tropicana is a major east-west corridor and one of RTC's highest-ridership non-Strip routes.

las_vegas_monorail.operator_history: Las Vegas Monorail Company (private, 2004-2020) → filed bankruptcy January 2020 → acquired by LVCVA July 2020 → resumed limited service October 2021

ridership.source: Las Vegas Monorail Company annual reports (pre-2020); LVCVA post-acquisition operational updates. 2019 figure from Monorail Company FY2019 report. 2023 figure estimated from partial LVCVA reporting and Las Vegas Review-Journal coverage of post-bankruptcy operations.

las_vegas_monorail.operating_hours: 07:00-02:00 Mon-Thu; 07:00-03:00 Fri-Sun (extended on major event weekends)
las_vegas_monorail.coverage_gap: Monorail runs parallel to but EAST of The Strip — hotels on the west side of the Strip (Caesars, Bellagio, Mirage, Wynn) require a cross-Strip walk. Does not serve Allegiant Stadium, Mandalay Bay, Sphere Las Vegas directly.
las_vegas_monorail.operational_status_note: As of April 2026, the monorail is operational under LVCVA management. It was closed during COVID (2020-2021) and underwent infrastructure maintenance during the transition period.
